Decompiling 0x47b140 (player_examine_nearby_vehicle) with tools/pack.py shows it reads/writes a per-player object flag through global DAT_008603b0 (a player-array base pointer, offset+0xc stride lookup then object+0x107 bit flag) - i.e. it manipulates player/object state, not script-compiler internals. hs_return/hs-arg-getter are generic dispatch plumbing shared by many hs external functions across modules (including these and the real hs compiler code further down), so calling them is not evidence of belonging to the 'hs' module itself. The trusted 0.8 game seeds should stand; these 5 functions (and the surrounding jump-table region, which likely accounts for the ~18KB gap before 0x482b20, per the 'jmp_table_adjust_size' name) belong to 'game', not 'hs'.
